findings.reason: the plan should name one deep aggregation whose indexed path is an option of it, so a change to the counted population cannot drift between the roadmap's and routing's readers.
findings.text: `section_attempts_by_plan` (full-plan read) and `_section_attempt_count_uncached` (indexed single-plan read, reckon/mcp_views.py:1705) are two aggregators over the same ledger+pointer population, sharing only `_group_section_attempts` and each embedding its own role predicate; the derivation the plan calls "computed once" therefore exists twice

findings.reason: the plan should extend the run-outcome owner `reckon/evidence.py` (which already holds `_VERDICT_ROLES` at :275 and whose docstring states a section attempt count reads that same population) instead of forking the aggregation into mcp_views.
findings.text: `resolve_section_routing` imports `section_attempt_count` from `reckon/mcp_views.py`, a presentation module, and `reckon/roadmap.py:56` imports `section_attempts_by_plan` from the same place, so core routing and roadmap logic reach into the views layer for a domain aggregate

findings.reason: §14's done-when ("the three readers count the same population") is unmet by its own census; the consolidation must name evidence.py:275 as the owner and reach all five literal sites, including the two raw SQL strings.
findings.text: the executable-role set `{"implement","test"}` is spelled as a bare literal at mcp_views.py:1605, :1643, :1720, :1724 and :1733, plus `_VERDICT_ROLES` (reckon/evidence.py:275) and `_IMPL_MOVE_ENFORCED_ROLES` (reckon/crew/promotion.py:7304, not the ~6910 the plan cites) — seven sites, against the four §14 names

findings.reason: the plan should reconcile §1's stored field with §4's derived ruling (drop it, mark it optional and non-authoritative, or rename it), rather than leave two quantities named attempts beside one another.
findings.text: `SectionRecord.attempts` is a *required* field whose description reads "Tool-owned launch count", while §4's ruling derives the count, reckon/_plan_html.py:379 documents `data-attempts` as "legacy, not the live count", and the reader never reads it, so every section record must carry a stored counter nothing writes and the plan calls authoritative

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the attempt-count derivation §4/§13 declare "computed once in Python" is two aggregation paths over the same run population in reckon/mcp_views.py, so the plan's one-figure promise is two readers that can drift.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the attempt derivation and the executable-role set are both duplicated outside their existing owner, reckon/evidence.py:275, which already holds the run-outcome population and documents that a section attempt count reads it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names and extends existing machinery rather than rebuilding it: the section-ref grammar from parse_plan_ref (reckon/_schema.py:274), the depends_on link grammar, CapabilityRequest, unwired_plan_finding, derive_impl_from_sections and gated_sections are all cited as the mechanisms it extends.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — SectionRecord.attempts is a required stored field described as the "Tool-owned launch count", a value the derived reader explicitly ignores, so the schema mandates a counter nothing writes.
